verdict_last_change.evidence: Shipped 2026-07-22, explicitly labelled measurable:false / 'this will NEVER be given a worked/worse verdict'. It is a code-level repair of the 07-20 diagnostic (email_field_engaged now fires on input as well as focus; getVisitorId falls back to an in-memory UUID when sessionStorage is blocked; tooling ordering fix) with no user-facing change and no conversion/verdict funnel touched, so it cannot be graded worked/worse and must not be retroactively claimed as a tested win. Its first real read is scheduled ~2026-08-05 and cannot be taken yet. This cycle CONFIRMS the pre-fix undercount is still visible: funnel-report 14d/until=2026-07-22 shows email_field_engaged=4 vs email_entered=103 (impossible for a true superset), so the fix was necessary and the sub-funnel is not yet usable. leaks_ranked.step: Claim page: scan (page view) -> gave email (the email gate)
leaks_ranked.rate: not freshly reproducible this cycle. Best available: session replay 59% (22 of 37 in-window claim recordings) never type a key; Supabase page_viewed->email_entered 26.7% (4 of 15 linkable, 66% of page_viewed rows unlinkable) is too new/biased to trust; PostHog cached capture from prior cycles ~44% (1864->826)
leaks_ranked.prior_rate: PostHog cached ~44% capture (stable across cycles); session-replay 'never types a key' ~67% (prior) vs 59% (this window, 22/37)
leaks_ranked.why_real: Largest single drop by headcount and stable across every cycle (~56-59% loss). Fresh session replay independently confirms most scanners never type: 22/37 = 59% zero-keypress this window. Reproduces across sources and windows, so it is a real leak, not noise.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: Biggest by headcount (~110 people/fortnight) but the WEAKEST per-person feed to reviews: each lost scanner is several probabilistic steps from a review (email -> ~46% video -> ~39% review-click), and replay shows a large share are instant/low-intent bounces (13 of 22 zero-key sessions were <15s active) who may never have wanted a next-order discount. It is also the most fenced step (see choice_reasoning).

leaks_ranked.step: Warm users: gave email -> started a video (in-app conversion)
leaks_ranked.why_real: ~54% of people who paid the email price never start the free video they were promised - a large, persistent drop among our WARMEST users, stable at 35-46% across windows. The +10.6pt move is NOT significant (p=0.220), so treat the level (~40-46%) as a standing leak, not as an improvement.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: High value-per-person to reviews: a video-start converts to a review click at ~39% on the in-app thank-you screen, so each recovered start is worth ~0.4 reviews - a far more direct feed than the claim gate. Audit-recommended target (never-attacked examples/occasion screen). BUT the losing sub-step (arrived->role vs role->message vs message->create) cannot be localized: message_written/create_clicked only started 2026-07-16 (8 vs 35 in-window, undercounted), PostHog is 403, and in-app replays are sparse (10) and mostly 1-3s. Cause is currently unverifiable. NAMED AS THE NEXT REAL PRIZE once the repaired diagnostic or restored PostHog access gives a localizable read (audit finding #2).

leaks_ranked.step: Review ask on non-thank-you surfaces (video-preview / share), video_started -> review click via preview
leaks_ranked.rate: 0 preview-sourced review clicks this window (of preview_opened=28)
leaks_ranked.why_real: The preview page is the peak-delight moment (creator watches the finished video, autoplay) yet produces ~0 review clicks despite real, recurring traffic (28-34 opens/window). Session replay confirms people REACH and ENGAGE the preview PAGE (e.g. 45s active, 13 clicks), which rules out the coarse 'never open the emailed video' reach failure. It does NOT, however, establish that arrivers scrolled past the autoplay video + the primary Send CTA + the <hr> divider to actually SEE the below-fold review ask - active-seconds as low as 7s are consistent with never reaching it. So replay leaves TWO indistinguishable ~0-producing causes on the table: 'saw the ask and ignored it' (copy/motivation) and 'never scrolled the below-divider ask into view' (below-fold visibility). Almost all review clicks (11/11 this window) come from the single in-app thank-you screen.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: Direct feed to reviews (the objective) and a currently-WASTED high-intent moment, so downside is ~0 (cannot do worse than ~0 clicks). Prize is modest in absolute terms (a few reviews/fortnight) but compounds, is on the objective directly, and is the safest untried visible bet available. THIS IS WHERE I SHIPPED.

biggest_leak: The biggest leak by headcount is the claim email gate, but I am deliberately NOT shipping there this cycle; I chose leak #3 (the ~0-converting preview-page review ask) for the visible experiment because it feeds reviews directly, is safe (downside ~0 on a currently-dead surface), is a genuinely untried mechanism, and it breaks four cycles of claim-page/instrumentation fixation. NOTE: I do NOT claim a verified cause here - the ask being generic is a code fact, but whether it is seen-and-ignored (H3) vs never-scrolled-into-view (H1b) is UNRESOLVED; the ship rests on the asymmetric-bet basis, not on a proven cause.

choice_reasoning.expected_value_to_reviews: The objective is reviews, and ~all reviews (11/11 this window) come from review-ask surfaces. The preview page is a second, better-timed ask (video just watched) to ~28 people/fortnight, of whom a meaningful (but not precisely known) share did NOT click review on the in-app screen - the ~61% in-app non-click figure is lag-truncated and overstates that un-converted pool, so treat it as a loose upper bound - currently yielding ~0. Even recovering a handful of clicks per fortnight is net-new honest reviews at ~zero risk, and it compounds. The claim gate, by contrast, is many probabilistic steps from a review per lost person; the warm-user step has higher per-person value but an unverifiable cause this cycle.
choice_reasoning.already_tried_here: Coverage map: 'Review ask: preview + share surfaces - 1 attempt. Reworked in June (non-destructive post-share highlight) -> still ~0 clicks.' That was ONE mechanism (a post-share pulse/scroll to draw the eye). One flat attempt does not retire the step; a different mechanism (motivational copy reframe at watch-time) is fair game and is what I propose.
choice_reasoning.what_history_suggests: Pattern across all changes: MECHANISM/motivation changes at warm, in-flow moments moved this funnel (2026-06-16 email-first + value-prop hero, +14pts into-app->video, held 3 weeks; making the in-app review ask the hero now produces almost all review clicks), while PRESENTATION reshuffles of a cold page did nothing (PR #8 claim-page layout, flat). Implication: bet on WHY-you-should copy at a high-intent moment (preview, post-watch), not on re-arranging a page. My change is a motivational reframe at the highest-delight moment - the kind that has worked here - so odds are better than a layout shuffle, though still unmeasurable at this traffic.
choice_reasoning.why_not_the_others: Claim gate (leak #1): fenced and unshippable this cycle - PR #8 layout redesign is spent ground, 'give the discount first' is owner-rejected, referencing the printed % is owner-rejected, and I found no NEW mechanism whose cause my evidence supports (replay shows a large share are low-intent instant bounces, not people repelled by the ask); it is also not freshly measurable (PostHog 403, page_viewed too new). Continuing to instrument it would be a fourth straight invisible cycle, explicitly disallowed. Warm-user step (leak #2): highest per-person value and audit-recommended, but the losing sub-step cannot be localized (in-app micro-steps undercounted, PostHog 403, replays sparse), so any fix would bet on an unverifiable cause - the exact mistake the last cycle was caught making. Preview (leak #3) is chosen not because its cause is verified (H3 vs H1b below-fold is unresolved) but because it is the only ranked leak addressable this cycle by a zero-downside, copy-only, reversible edit on a currently-dead (~0) surface - an asymmetric bet, not a cause-proven fix.

findings_addressed: Finding #1 (minor): the new event review_section_viewed was not registered in analytics-events.js (the single source of truth). ADDRESSED - added EVENTS.REVIEW_SECTION_VIEWED = 'review_section_viewed' to analytics-events.js FIRST, then mirrored it inline in video-preview.html as a const referenced by observeReviewSection (matching how the other pages mirror event strings). Verified under a mocked DOM that the event posts to /api/track with event=review_section_viewed, phase=preview, and source video_preview_buyer / video_preview_receiver, and that track.js writes it (no whitelist; it does not trigger Klaviyo since it is not review_clicked/share_completed). A future H1b-vs-H3 read can now rely on it.

Finding #2 (minor): this is honest small polish and it defers the higher-per-person leak #2 (warm users gave-email -> started-video, the never-attacked examples/occasion screen). ADDRESSED - labelling is kept honest (measurable:false, business_impact:false), and leak #2 is explicitly named as the next real prize (in leaks_ranked and in the changelog) once the repaired claim/in-app diagnostic or restored PostHog access gives a localizable read on WHICH in-app sub-step loses people, so it is not quietly dropped.

change.title: Warmer, honest review ask on the 'your video is ready' screen (the moment they just watched it)
change.targets: The review ask on the video-preview page (the creator's preview/share screen), both before and after they hit Send. Metric: preview-sourced review clicks (source=video_preview_buyer / video_preview_receiver), which is ~0 today.
change.expected_effect: A small, likely-unmeasurable increase in review clicks from the preview screen - net-new honest reviews on top of the ones we already get from the in-app thank-you screen. Plus a new behind-the-scenes counter that will, within a few cycles, tell us whether people even scroll far enough to SEE this review ask.
change.why_it_helps: Right now, at the exact moment someone has just watched the video they made, we ask for a review with generic seller-speak ('we would really appreciate a quick review') - and almost nobody clicks. This reword speaks to their pride in what they just made and simply invites an honest review, which is the kind of warm, well-timed nudge that has moved this before.
changes_in_plain_words: The review box on the 'your video is ready' screen now reads 'Proud of the video you just made? If it brought a smile, a quick honest review helps other gift-givers find us' with a 'Leave an honest review' button - instead of the old 'Made You Smile? We would really appreciate a quick review'.
After someone taps Send, the same box now says 'Sent! Proud of what you made?' instead of the old 'Sent! Made you smile?', so the warmer wording shows whether they share first or not.
It reads more premium: the stacked star and heart emoji are gone and the tone is warm rather than pushy.
It now uses the words 'honest review', which keeps us squarely inside Amazon's rules (the old wording did not).

Behind the scenes, we quietly record the first time the review box actually scrolls onto someone's screen - no one sees anything - so a later check can tell us whether people are missing the ask entirely or seeing it and passing.

previews.label: the 'your video is ready' preview screen (the review box, below the Send button)

change.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: Converters here give unpaid effort (writing an Amazon review) in exchange for the emotional payoff of pride/gratitude - there is no material reward, and offering one would violate Amazon TOS. At the preview moment the user's goal is to SEND the video to the recipient; the review ask is a secondary, generic request competing with that goal, so it only lands for the small subset already moved by pride. Anchoring the copy on the video they just made is an attempt to raise that pride signal at the moment it is highest.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A meaningful share of preview arrivers have NOT already clicked review on the in-app screen (WEAKLY supported: the ~61% in-app non-click figure is lag-truncated and overstated, so it is a loose upper bound on the un-converted second-chance pool, not a firm floor).

Preview arrivers actually scroll to and read the below-divider review ask (UNVERIFIED TODAY, but the ride-along review_section_viewed instrument is designed to answer exactly this in a future cycle: if the event fires the ask is seen, if it stays ~0 it is not (H1b) and copy cannot help).
Delight/pride-anchored, honest copy raises review intent more than the current generic seller-oriented copy at this moment (unproven - the bet).

The reworded copy actually reaches BOTH pre-share and post-share viewers (SECURED by this build: the rewrite is applied to renderBuyerPreview, renderReceiverPreview, AND the highlightReviewAsk post-share override, so sharers no longer fall back to the old generic heading).
The change does not weaken the primary share CTA (guaranteed: copy-only edit inside the existing review-section, below share; the share button is untouched).
change.second_order_effects: The primary CTA on preview is SHARE, which drives the recipient loop (video.html -> potentially more videos/reviews); the review ask must stay subordinate to it. This change is copy-only inside the existing review-section below the share button (plus the post-share heading override), so it does not move, resize, or compete with the share CTA - share is unaffected. Editing the highlightReviewAsk override changes only the words in the same in-place card that already exists post-share (the June non-destructive pulse/scroll behaviour is preserved), so no post-share behaviour regresses. The ride-along review_section_viewed event is a single fire-once logFunnel write per preview session (same /api/track path already used by preview_opened), negligible write volume and no user-facing effect. It does not touch the in-app thank-you review ask (the current review engine, 11/11 clicks) or the Klaviyo email-redirect path (0 this window, 2 prior), so those review sources are unchanged. Bringing the word 'honest' into the on-page ask keeps us squarely inside Amazon TOS and consistent across pre-share and post-share states.
change.strongest_case_against: A sceptic who knows this business would say: 'Preview review clicks are ~0 because these users already saw and declined the in-app review ask minutes earlier - the moment is spent, and the surface was already attacked once in June and stayed dead. You are polishing a corpse.' My honest answer concedes part of this: I CANNOT prove the audience is un-converted (the ~61% in-app non-click figure is lag-truncated and overstates the second-chance pool) and I CANNOT prove today the below-divider ask is even seen (no scroll data). I ship anyway because: (1) preview is a genuinely better-timed ask when it IS seen (they have now WATCHED the video, which the in-app screen never showed them); (2) the June attempt was a different mechanism (a post-share attention pulse), not a motivational copy reframe, so this is not a repeat; (3) the surface is at ~0, so a copy-only reversible edit has downside bounded at ~0 while upside is open. On the 'cannot even learn' charge: the ride-along review_section_viewed instrument means a future cycle CAN separate H1b (never seen) from H3 (seen, ignored), so the surface stops absorbing blind ships. No worked/worse verdict on the copy without a SIGNIFICANT significance.mjs print.

tradeoff.gained: Potentially a few net-new honest reviews per fortnight from a currently-wasted, high-delight surface (now reaching BOTH pre- and post-share viewers), with the ask brought into explicit 'honest review' TOS alignment. PLUS a durable diagnostic gain independent of the copy bet: the review_section_viewed instrument resolves whether this dead surface is a visibility (H1b) or motivation (H3) problem, so no future cycle has to guess blind here again.
tradeoff.risked: Near-nothing. The surface already produces ~0 preview-sourced review clicks (0 this window, 2 prior), so there is no working number to break. The share CTA is untouched (copy-only, below share); the highlightReviewAsk edit changes only wording in the same post-share card that already exists (pulse/scroll behaviour preserved); the review_section_viewed write is one fire-once event on the existing /api/track path; and the in-app thank-you review engine (11/11 clicks this window) and the Klaviyo email-redirect review path (0 this window, 2 prior) are not modified.
unverified_assumptions: Whether the below-divider review ask is ever scrolled into view (H1b) - I have NO scroll-depth data TODAY, so at ship time this remains unverified; but the ride-along review_section_viewed instrument added in this build is designed to answer it within a few cycles, converting this from a permanent unknown into a measurable read.

Whether preview arrivers are disproportionately people who already clicked review in-app (redundancy, H2) - cannot be linked per-person at this N; only weakly bounded by the ~61% in-app non-click rate, which is itself lag-truncated and overstates the un-converted pool.

OWNER FACT-CORRECTION (surfaced, not acted on): claim traffic now arrives with code=GOTYOU30 & source=insert|box (visible in ~all in-window claim session-recording start_urls), which CONTRADICTS the FUNNEL_CONTEXT [FACT] that only ?sku arrives. If GOTYOU30 is a real multi-use printed code, it weakens the 'discount is the price of the email' premise that fences leak #1. This build does not touch the claim page and does not rely on it; the owner should resolve it before the leak-#1 fencing rationale is relied on again.

change.differs_from_past_attempt: Differs from the June preview change (coverage map: 'non-destructive post-share highlight' - a post-share pulse/scroll to draw the eye): that was an ATTENTION/animation mechanism; this is a MOTIVATION/copy mechanism (anchor on the just-watched video + explicit 'honest'), applied at watch-time not only post-share. Differs from PR #8 (claim-page LAYOUT redesign - a different page and a reshuffle, not copy). Differs from the owner-rejected proposals (give the discount code before the email; reference the printed %) - it touches neither the discount nor the print. Differs from the owner rejection closed 2026-07-21 ('add a gentle honest-review link to the video-ready EMAIL') - that is the Klaviyo email surface and proposes a NEW link; this rewords an EXISTING on-page review link on the preview page, adds no new link, and touches no email.
change.verification: node --check passed on analytics-events.js and on the extracted video-preview inline script. Booted the app (PORT=3939 node --experimental-websocket server.js) and fetched /video-preview.html?id=test -> HTTP 200 containing the new buyer+receiver copy (2 headings, 2 buttons), the post-share heading 'Sent! Proud of what you made?', the review_section_viewed constant + call, and observeReviewSection wired into both renders; the OLD 'Made You Smile' and 'Leave a Review' strings return count 0. Drove the REAL edited code under a mocked DOM: observeReviewSection fired review_section_viewed EXACTLY ONCE per session for buyer (source video_preview_buyer, phase preview, role buyer) and receiver (video_preview_receiver) even when the IntersectionObserver callback ran twice; highlightReviewAsk set the post-share heading to 'Sent! Proud of what you made?'; trackReviewClick still logged review_clicked with the correct source and returned false. No Supabase test rows were created (the behavioral test mocked the network). Rendered BEFORE/AFTER mobile PNGs of the preview screen (exact page CSS) under cycle-artifacts/2026-07-22/ and visually confirmed the copy change.
change.commit_message: feat(preview): delight-anchored honest review ask + review_section_viewed instrument

pr_body:
## What this does

This reworks the review ask on the **'your video is ready' preview screen** - the moment someone has just watched the video they made - so it speaks to their pride in what they made and simply invites an **honest review**, instead of the old generic 'Made You Smile? We would really appreciate a quick review'. It also quietly starts recording whether people even scroll far enough to see that ask.

**Before:** '⭐ Made You Smile? / We would really appreciate a quick review - it only takes 30 seconds. Thank You! ❤️' with a 'Leave a Review' button.
**After:** 'Proud of the video you just made? / If it brought a smile, a quick honest review helps other gift-givers find us.' with a 'Leave an honest review' button. After they hit Send, the same box now reads 'Sent! Proud of what you made?'. The stacked emoji are gone; the wording is warm, not pushy, and now contains 'honest review' (which keeps us inside Amazon's rules - the old wording did not).

See the attached BEFORE/AFTER photos of the exact screen.

## How the last change did

The last shipped change (2026-07-22, harden the claim-page email-gate measurement) is **measurement-only and unmeasurable by design** - it has no customer-facing effect and cannot be graded worked/worse. Its first real read is scheduled ~2026-08-05. The last change that DID target a customer conversion (the 2026-07-06 create-screen fix) is **still not measurable**: gave-email -> started-a-video moved 23/39 -> 28/46, +1.9 points, p=0.859 (`node tools/significance.mjs 23 39 28 46`) - deep inside the noise floor at this traffic. Not a win, not a loss.

One number I am **reporting but explicitly NOT claiming as a win**: video-started -> review-click read 3/24 (12.5%) prior vs 11/28 (39.3%) now, which the significance test flags as SIGNIFICANT (+26.8 points, p=0.030). No shipped change targeted that step, and it is a same-window ratio that the changelog warns is confounded (review clicks arrive days later via email reminders, so a frozen window is unreliable). It is not attributable to anything and is not a graded result.

## The leaks, ranked

1. **Claim email gate** - biggest by headcount (~110 people/fortnight never give an email) but the weakest per-person feed to reviews, and it is fenced this cycle (past layout redesign was flat; 'give the discount first' and 'reference the printed %' are owner-rejected; PostHog query access is down again with a 403). Not shipped here.
2. **Warm users: gave email -> started a video** (~46%, 28 of 61; not a significant change from 35%). Highest value per person, but we cannot yet tell WHICH in-app step loses people (those sub-steps only started logging on 2026-07-16 and are undercounted, and PostHog is down). Betting a fix here would be guessing at an unverifiable cause - so it is deferred, and kept named as the next real prize.
3. **Review ask on the preview screen** - ~0 review clicks despite real traffic (28 preview opens this window). This is what I shipped: a direct feed to reviews, on a currently-dead surface, so the downside is ~0.

## Why this one

Almost all our reviews (11 of 11 this window) come from review-ask screens, and the preview screen is a *better-timed* ask than the one that works - the person has just watched their finished video. Session recordings confirm people reach and engage that page. What they don't tell us is whether anyone scrolls far enough to see the review box (it sits below the video and the Send button). So this change does two things: (a) rewords the ask to be warmer and pride-anchored - the kind of well-timed motivational nudge that has moved this before - and (b) adds a tiny behind-the-scenes counter that records the first time the review box scrolls onto screen, so a later check can finally tell us whether people are missing it entirely or seeing it and passing.

**Honest caveat:** at ~28 preview opens a fortnight, a change here will read 'not yet measurable' for many cycles - the value is in compounding small wins, not one provable jump. I will never claim this worked without a SIGNIFICANT significance-test result.

## What the auditor said, and how I responded

The independent auditor **approved** the plan with two minor notes. (1) Register the new event in the single source-of-truth file first - done: I added `review_section_viewed` to analytics-events.js before using it, and confirmed under test that it records with the right screen and buyer/receiver tag. (2) Don't quietly drop the higher-value warm-user leak - it stays named as the next real prize once we can see which in-app step loses people.

## How I verified it

Booted the app and loaded the preview screen: it returns 200 with the new buyer and receiver copy, the new post-share wording, and the new counter wired in; the old wording is gone. Drove the real edited code under a simulated browser: the counter fires exactly once per visit (buyer and receiver, correctly tagged) even if the screen scrolls in and out, the post-share heading updates, and the review button still works and still records the click. No test data was written to the database. Rendered before/after mobile photos of the exact screen.

## What to re-measure, and when

Around **2026-08-19** (≥4 weeks): count review clicks that came from the preview screen (broken out by buyer vs receiver) over a fresh 14-day window versus the prior one, and run the significance test on them (the exact commands are recorded in the changelog). Also compare the new 'review box seen' counter against how many people opened the preview screen - if the box IS being seen but clicks stay ~0, that is a real finding that this copy, once seen, does not motivate; if the box is rarely seen, the next move is visibility/placement, not copy. Until that counter has data, a flat ~0 here means nothing and must not be read as 'the copy failed'.
telegram_summary: Last change (claim-page measurement fix) is measurement-only - can't be graded worked/worse; first read ~Aug 5. The last real conversion change is still noise (p=0.86).
